This works because of the translucency. First, try to focus on just one dot, it's hard with this one because the frame rate isn't great, but try. The dot isn't moving in three dimensions, it's just going back and forth.

Now we need to talk about neurology. The brain has a built in facial recognition mechanism; a small portion of the visual system who's processing power is entirely dedicated to facial recognition. Fun fact: domestic dogs raised since puppies develop a similar specialized processing mechanism for human faces. Keep in mind that 3D is an illusion, and all light energy is absorbed on a 2d plane. When you see the image of a face, this dedicated processor automatically detects and labels the face, then constructs 3D for it.

Next, our brains have a system for maintaining the consistency of a scene. Motion between "frames" of perception is produced in another dedicated area of the visual system, and it has been demonstrated that individuals with either damage or deformity here experience vision as a "stop motion" without conserved motion. Once a 3D face is recognized, 3D is generated for the rest of the figure, and motion is generated that maintains the perception of this 3D model.

So what does this all mean? The direction you see her spin will correlate with the direction the "face dots" where moving when you first viewed the image. If you want to make her spin the other way, focus above her head and only look down when you know a dot that is part of the "face" array is moving the direction you want her to spin.

Edit: the eyes are very decernable in the peripheral, use them to know when to refocus on the image and direct her spin, if you get good at it you can constantly flip her spin back and forth.

Sitting Back vs. Down in the Squat: Much Ado About Very Little

Good read. About a year ago I switched up my cues for my squat, and it made a huge difference.

For me, the "sit back" cue would cause me to arch my low back, and put my spine in a bad position. I ended up replacing that cue with two separate ones. The first is "hips under", which helps me tighten up my abs; and "hips away", which helps me start my movement hinging at my hips first.

I guess that is kinda like saying "sit down".

Is there a better explanation?

I just moved off the smith machine, but I'm pretty sure I arch my back during squats and I'd prefer to master form than weight.

http://www.precisionnutrition.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2011/07/flexion-extension-and-neutral-spine.png

This might help more than me trying to explain. For me, the sit back cue was causing me to overarch, like the middle picture. My proprioception (the minds ability to perceive the position of a body part) was incorrect.

If you are concerned about your form, I highly recommend video taping yourself squatting.

Evernote is great because I have a plain old classic feature rich desktop application. I don't use apps because they are crippled desktop applications.

I did uninstall the Windows Evernote app on my windows phone since it insisted on location data. Every app that requests location data that I cannot disable I uninstall.
